_comment: Three different variances. The published CIs measure only the first. Quoting a task-resampling interval next to a claim that depends on the other two invites the reader to assume a precision the design does not support.

task_resampling.what_it_measures: redraw the 800 tasks from the same generator

sampling_marginal.what_it_measures: same weights, same pool, different decode budget
sampling_marginal.caveat: n=1 pair of runs at two budgets, not a variance estimate. It bounds the effect from below by showing a single budget change moves R_w by this much.

eval_pool_seed.what_it_measures: same weights, same budget, different draw of tasks
eval_pool_seed.caveat: Establishes only that the CHAMPION's R_w is stable across eval pools. It says nothing about the comparison: DeepSeek was not run on these seeds, and these are 300-task pools while the headline is an 800-task pool. Reading the champion's mean here against DeepSeek's seed-777 score would be exactly the unmatched comparison this work exists to remove.

training_seed.what_it_measures: same recipe, same data, different training seed
training_seed.caveat: The two runs differ by 0.18 R_w, but they are not a controlled seed comparison -- the sibling's weights were overwritten and it cannot be re-scored. PRE-REGISTRATION section 6 requires >=3 training seeds and the claim holding at mean - 1 SD. Until those run, no single-run claim in either direction is supportable.
